headline: Figma Goes All-In on AI
subheadline: Big Figma updates this month including ChatGPT Images 2.0 and new Figma-Context-MCP features — plus Cursor's parallel agents are here and design systems are getting the AI treatment everywhere.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma adds ChatGPT Images 2.0 across Design, Draw, Slides, Buzz, FigJam & Weave
sections.description: OpenAI's newest image model is now baked into Make Image and Edit Image across basically every Figma surface — Design, Draw, Slides, Buzz, FigJam, and Weave. This is a meaningful upgrade to the generative image quality inside your existing workflows. Worth checking if it changes how you handle placeholder assets or exploration in your white-label sport apps.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma Made a Huge Step Forward in AI Design — April 2026
sections.description: A developer's breakdown of the full scope of Figma's April AI push. Useful as a quick audit of what's changed this month — you'll want to know which new capabilities might affect your design system architecture or component workflows, especially with your MCP integration in play.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Figma-Context-MCP v0.9.0 — now with component property support
sections.description: The open-source Figma-Context-MCP just shipped v0.9.0 with BOOLEAN and TEXT component property support, plus proxy support for managed networks. This directly matters for your MCP + Claude integration work — component properties flowing through MCP means Claude can now understand and manipulate more of your design system's logic layer.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Cursor April 2026: Tiled Agents, Self-Hosted Cloud & Better Scoping
sections.description: Cursor now lets you run multiple agents in parallel with a tiled layout, plus self-hosted cloud agents and file search filters for tighter code scoping. The parallel agents thing is a real workflow shift if you're vibe-coding across frontend and backend simultaneously. Worth a quick scan of the changelog.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: AI-Augmented Design Systems
sections.description: Design systems are shifting from static component libraries to AI-augmented systems that embed accessibility at the component level (47% now include comprehensive a11y guidelines) and use AI to automate token generation, variant creation, and cross-platform consistency. This is the exact trajectory your white-label sport apps design system is on — the strategic framing here could help you articulate its value to leadership when you're back.

sections.label: Listen
sections.title: Claude Code: What's New in April 2026 (5 Updates You Need)
sections.description: Walkthrough of Claude Code's latest April updates. Given you're building with Claude Code daily, this is worth a stroller listen to make sure you haven't missed anything — particularly around the week 15 release that landed mid-April with potential workflow improvements for your MCP integration.

sections.label: Did you know
sections.title: 47% of design systems now include comprehensive accessibility guidelines at the component level
sections.description: Up significantly from prior years. If your white-label design system doesn't have a11y baked into the component spec layer yet, you're falling behind nearly half the industry. Good ammunition for prioritizing this when you return — especially since AI can now auto-audit and suggest a11y improvements at the token level.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: With MCP now reading component properties, what should Claude be able to *do* with your design system?
sections.description: Figma-Context-MCP v0.9.0 can now pass boolean and text component properties to Claude. This opens up real possibilities: auto-generating variant documentation, validating design system usage, or even having Claude suggest which components to use for a given screen. What's the first high-value use case you'd ship for your team?
